snip.s: Principles of Microbiology and Parasitology MCQs

snip.t: Trichomonas vaginalis is a protozoan parasite responsible for trichomoniasis, a sexually transmitted infection (STI).
snip.s: Trichomonas Vaginalis: Understanding Trichomoniasis, Symptoms — Notes

snip.t: Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) with a prevalence of 5%–75%, depending on the population:5% in general hospital patients.
Infection: cervicitis, endometritis, trichomoniasis or chlamydia (also a retained foreign body such as a pessary)
Trichomoniasis: Trichomonas vaginalis, a protozoan parasite causing frothy, malodorous vaginal discharge and dysuria.
Intracellular edema, resulting in chicken-like epithelial cells (a hallmark of trichomoniasis).

qs.q: Why is it crucial to treat both sexual partners simultaneously when managing a case of trichomoniasis?
o: To prevent immediate reinfection between partners
To activate dormant systemic immune responses
To prevent development of parasite encystment
To eradicate the organism from respiratory tracts
qs.e: Because trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection, treating both sexual partners simultaneously is essential to prevent rapid reinfection. Failure to treat partners leads to recurring clinical episodes.

qs.q: What is a key consideration when administering metronidazole to a pregnant patient diagnosed with trichomoniasis?
o: It should only be used if delivery is imminent
It is completely contraindicated throughout pregnancy
It is safely administered during second and third trimesters
It must be given intravenously regardless of gestation
qs.e: Metronidazole is considered safe for use in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy. During the first trimester, treatment is typically deferred unless symptoms are severe due to safety precautions.

qs.q: An infectious disease specialist is reviewing diagnostic options for a patient with suspected trichomoniasis whose initial saline wet mount was negative. Which diagnostic technique represents the traditional reference method yielding high sensitivity?
o: Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay testing
Rapid antigen immunochromatography
Culture using specialized liquid media
Direct Fluorescent Antibody staining
qs.e: Culture is traditionally considered the standard reference method when microscopy is negative, yielding high sensitivity when grown under anaerobic conditions. Antigen and antibody tests generally show lower sensitivity than direct organism growth.

qs.q: A public health clinic treats a woman for trichomoniasis with a single 2 g oral dose of metronidazole. What is the critical additional instruction that must be given to ensure successful management and prevent recurrence?
o: Simultaneous treatment of her sexual partners
Abstinence from sexual contact for exactly six weeks
Routine follow-up culture every forty-eight hours
Daily intake of probiotic supplements for two weeks
qs.e: Both sexual partners must be treated simultaneously to effectively prevent reinfection and clear the organism from the community. Partner management is a core principle in controlling trichomoniasis transmission.

qs.q: A pregnant woman in her first trimester is diagnosed with symptomatic trichomoniasis. According to treatment guidelines, when should pharmacotherapy with metronidazole be initiated?
o: Immediately, regardless of symptom severity
Only if her symptoms are severe
Postpartum to avoid any embryonic exposure
Only after transitioning to the second trimester
qs.e: Metronidazole is considered safe in the second and third trimesters, but in the first trimester, treatment is administered only if symptoms are severe. Routine asymptomatic treatment is typically delayed.

qs.q: A patient presents with persistent symptoms of trichomoniasis despite completing a standard course of oral metronidazole. Which of the following is an appropriate management strategy for this resistant case?
o: Switching to a 14-day course of oral amoxicillin
Repeating the initial 2 g single-dose metronidazole regimen
Applying topical antifungal creams directly to the cervix
Switching to tinidazole or increasing the metronidazole dose
qs.e: Management of resistant cases involves increasing the metronidazole dose, switching to tinidazole, or utilizing intravenous metronidazole in severe cases. Antibiotics like amoxicillin are ineffective against protozoan parasites.

qs.q: A patient with suspected trichomoniasis has a negative saline wet mount, prompting the laboratory to set up a culture. What are the optimal atmospheric and temperature conditions required to achieve the best growth results?
o: Anaerobic conditions at 35-37°C
High carbon dioxide conditions at room temperature
Aerobic conditions at 20-22°C
Microaerophilic conditions at 42°C
qs.e: Trichomonas vaginalis grows best at 35-37°C under anaerobic conditions with an optimal pH of 5.5-6.0. Standard aerobic or cold incubator settings will fail to support optimal parasitic replication.

qs.q: During a gynecological examination, a clinician observes characteristic physical signs of a urogenital parasitic infection in a female patient. Which set of findings is classically associated with female trichomoniasis?
o: Painful vesicular lesions, clear exudate, and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Pruritic vaginitis, greenish-yellow discharge, and strawberry mucosa
Hyperkeratotic plaques, thick white curd-like discharge, and normal pH
Profuse watery gray discharge with a strong fishy odor upon whiff test
qs.e: Classic clinical features in females include pruritic vaginitis, a greenish-yellow discharge, strawberry mucosa, and dysuria. Vesicles indicate herpes simplex, white curd-like discharge indicates candidiasis, and a fishy odor indicates bacterial vaginosis.
